purpose_planets_compare: Compare the planets using size, Sun distance or orbital pace. Choose a reference planet, try an example, then move elapsed time to explore their different year lengths.
planet_size_view: Planet widths on the same scale
planet_distance_view: Mean Sun distances on the same scale
planet_orbit_view: Orbit pace over the same elapsed time
planet_size_help: Disk widths follow equatorial diameters. The surface patterns are illustrative; the space between the disks is just for comparison.
planet_distance_help: Both lines start at the Sun and use the same distance scale. Planet markers are enlarged. AU is the average Earth–Sun distance.
planet_orbit_help: Both planets start aligned. Motion uses their reference year lengths at a steady pace. Tracks are separated and bodies enlarged for clarity; these are teaching positions.
planet_lab_intro: Choose what to compare, select a planet, then change the reference. Try Earth & Jupiter for size or Neptune’s long year for orbital pace.
planet_rows_help: Select a row to choose a planet. All eight bars use one scale; the dot marks each endpoint.
planet_day_help: Spin period measures one turn against the distant stars. A solar day runs from one local noon to the next. Retrograde means opposite Earth’s spin direction.
planet_data_date: Published March 18, 2025. Rounded reference values; the diagrams compare measurements and orbital pace.
